editorial:
Imagine walking into a room and seeing a regular couple arguing, but then you hear these fancy lines from a play written a hundred years ago playing in the background. That is the weird and cool vibe of this movie. You get to see how men and women deal with love and power in a modern setting, while the director uses an old script to show that people haven't really changed that much over time. It feels like a mix between a real-life documentary and a stage play, making you wonder if the love we talk about today is just a fake idea passed down from the past.

You will probably notice that the acting feels very raw and natural, which helps the movie stay grounded even when the dialogue gets a bit heavy. Some parts might feel a bit slow because it focuses more on talking than action, but it is a great pick if you like stories that make you think. If you want to check it out, try searching for a digital rental on Apple TV or look for a high-quality 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing that the cycle of fighting and misunderstanding between the man and woman never truly ends. Instead of a happy ending or a big fight, it leaves you with the feeling that their relationship is stuck. The final scenes link back to the old play, proving that the struggles of love from 1922 are still happening today. It ends on a quiet note, leaving you to think about your own relationships.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep conversations and indie films.
